title: Competing triangular and stripe supersolid orders in a dipolar quantum gas
authors: Karthik Chandrashekara, Christian Gölzhäuser, Lily Platt, Jianshun Gao, Julian Kusch, Lennart Hoenen, Manon Ballu, Wyatt Kirkby, Lauriane Chomaz
abstract: Supersolids are exotic quantum states in which long-range phase coherence coexists, and may interplay, with emergent spatial orders. A particularly rich phase diagram featuring several competing spatial orders is predicted for dipolar supersolids with two-dimensional crystals, yet the experimental observation of this structural variety has remained limited. Here we experimentally form competing triangular and stripe density-modulated states in a quantum gas of highly magnetic atoms confined in a surfboard-shaped trap by tuning contact interaction strength and dipole orientation. We define a structural order parameter and study its statistical behavior. Thereby, we identify both the triangular and stripe phases and the transition between them, the associated critical behavior being marked by enhanced non-Gaussian fluctuations. Furthermore, we observe each spatial structure in both the phase-coherent supersolid regime and the phase-incoherent insulating one, near and far from the unmodulated-to-modulated transition, respectively. Our results establish a versatile platform in which multiple phases of the two-dimensional-supersolid phase diagram, and more generally, intertwined symmetry-breaking phenomena, can be investigated.
summary: This paper reports experimental evidence for competing triangular and stripe supersolid orders in a dipolar quantum gas. By tuning external parameters like dipole orientation and interaction strength, the researchers mapped out a complex phase diagram. The study uses advanced spectral analysis to characterize the structural transitions and confirms the interplay between spatial order and global phase coherence.
main_problem: The study investigates the competition and coexistence of multiple spatial orders (triangular and stripe) in dipolar supersolids, and how global phase coherence interacts with this structural order.
main_result: The authors experimentally formed and characterized both competing triangular and stripe density-modulated states, identifying the structural phase transition between them and observing these structures in both phase-coherent and phase-incoherent regimes.
method: Structural analysis was performed by computing the 2D power spectrum of in-situ density distributions, while phase coherence was probed using time-of-flight measurements.
model_or_system: The system is a dipolar quantum gas of highly magnetic atoms (e.g., Dy) confined in a surfboard-shaped trap. Control is achieved by tuning the contact interaction strength ($a_s$) and the dipole tilt angle ($\alpha$).
key_observables: Structural order parameter, 2D power spectrum $S(\mathbf{k})$, and the ratio of phase to modulation amplitudes ($A_\phi/A_M$) from TOF images.
important_parameters: Dipole tilt angle ($\alpha$) and contact interaction strength ($a_s$), which control the transition between triangular and stripe phases.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on defining structural order parameters from the power spectrum and distinguishing between different spatial arrangements based on spectral signatures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental protocol and a phase diagram ($\alpha$ vs. $a_s$) showing the predicted states, alongside in-situ images and power spectra confirming the presence of triangular and stripe patterns.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of establishing the physical platform, presenting theoretical predictions via simulations, and then detailing experimental measurements using structural and coherence diagnostics to map out the complex phase diagram.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly controllable platform to study intertwined symmetry-breaking phenomena in 2D supersolids, offering quantitative measurements of critical behavior associated with competing crystalline orders.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Protocol and Phase Diagram (a) Sketch of the gas geometry (left panel). The gas is confined in a shallow surfboard trap with tighter confinement along z. A uniform magnetic field is applied in the xz plane with tunable mag- nitude B and tilt angle α. In the experiment, we ramp B and α in 100 ms, hold for 30 ms (right panels). (b) Phase diagram as a function of as and α constructed from TeGPE simulations with experimental settings. Alongside exemplary ground-state density profiles, cut at z = 0 (parameters identi- fied by symbols). Unmodulated, triangular, and stripe states are identified from such profiles (App. D).

S(k) is normalized to the peak at k = 0; the color scale is clipped to the maximum of the finite-k peaks in the range kρ ∈[1.3, 2.7] µm−1 for visibility.

FIG. 3. Statistics of the structural order parameter The nth-order cumulants κn of the order parameter R extracted from the power spectra of 30 independent experimental shots for varying B and α with (a) n = 1 (mean), (b) n = 2 (variance), (c) n = 3 and (d) n = 4 cumulants. The solid white line highlights the boundary between modulated and unmodulated states extracted from the S(k)-amplitude analysis (App. F).
